apple|aubandpass.about: AUBandpass is Apple's band-pass filter: it keeps a band of frequencies around a center point and attenuates everything above and below it. Use it for telephone or radio-style thinning, for isolating a frequency region to listen to it, or for sound design. Center Frequency sets the middle of the passed band in Hz, and Bandwidth sets how wide the band is (in cents; smaller values give a narrower, more nasal result).
apple|aubandpass.name: AUBandpass

apple|audelay.about: AUDelay is Apple’s stereo AudioUnit delay that repeats the incoming signal after a set time, with the repeats filtered and controlled by feedback. It is useful for simple echoes, rhythmic repeats, widening, and adding space or texture to vocals, drums, bass, or loops. Set Delay Time in seconds to the desired repeat interval; common jobs may use 0.06 to 0.5 s for tight slaps or 0.2 to 1 s for wider echoes. Dry/Wet Mix balances original against repeats, around 10 to 30 for subtle support or 40 to 70 for obvious effect. Feedback controls repeat strength, about 10 to 40 for short repeats or 50 to 80 for longer trails; keep below 100 to avoid runaway. Lowpass Cutoff Frequency darkens repeats, 8000 to 15000 Hz for natural decay, lower for muffled tails.
apple|audelay.name: AUDelay

apple|audistortion.about: AUDistortion is Apple's multi-effect distortion unit, combining a short delay, decimation (bit and sample-rate reduction), polynomial waveshaping, ring modulation and a soft clipper. It is for lo-fi, glitchy, metallic or heavily distorted sound design rather than subtle saturation. Each section has its own mix control (Delay Mix, Decimation Mix, Polynomial Mix, Ring Mod Mix); Decimation and Rounding control the lo-fi crunch, Linear Term, Squared Term and Cubic Term shape the harmonic distortion, Ring Mod Freq 1 and Ring Mod Freq 2 set the ring-modulator tones, Soft Clip Gain sets the clipper stage, and Wet/Dry Mix blends the whole effect with the original.
apple|audistortion.name: AUDistortion

apple|audynamicsprocessor.about: AUDynamicsProcessor is Apple's combined compressor and downward expander: it reduces the level of signal above a threshold and can further lower signal that falls below a second, lower threshold. Use it to even out the level of voice or instruments and, with expansion, to push down low-level noise between phrases. Compression Threshold sets where compression starts and Headroom sets how much room is left above it (less headroom means stronger compression); Expansion Threshold and Expansion Ratio control the downward expander (a ratio of 1 leaves it off); Attack Time and Release Time set the response speed, and Master Gain sets the output level.
apple|audynamicsprocessor.name: AUDynamicsProcessor

apple|aufilter.about: AUFilter is Apple's five-section equalizer: a low filter, three parametric bands and a high filter. Use it for general tone shaping such as removing rumble, cutting mud or harshness, or adding presence. Low Filter Type and High Filter Type choose the type of the edge sections, with Low Frequency/Low Gain and High Frequency/High Gain setting them; each parametric band has Center Freq, Center Gain and Bandwidth (1, 2 and 3).
apple|aufilter.name: AUFilter

apple|augraphiceq.about: AUGraphicEQ is Apple's graphic equalizer, with one gain slider per fixed frequency band (the parameters are named by their band, from 20.0 Hz to 20000.0 Hz). Use it for broad tonal balancing: cutting boom or mud, softening harshness, or adding brightness. Number of Bands switches between the 10-band and 31-band layouts; raise or lower the individual band parameters in dB, using gentle moves on neighbouring bands for smooth curves.
apple|augraphiceq.name: AUGraphicEQ

apple|auhighshelffilter.about: AUHighShelfFilter is an Apple AudioUnit high-shelf filter that boosts or cuts high-frequency content above the selected cutoff point. It is useful for brightening dull recordings, adding air to cymbals, vocals, or synths, and taming harsh or brittle high-end energy. Cutoff Frequency, in Hz, ranges from 10000 to 22050 and sets where the shelving begins; use near 10000 Hz for a broader high-end lift or reduction, or above 15000 Hz to affect mostly the top end. Gain, in dB, ranges from -40 to 40; start around +6 dB for brightness or air, and -6 dB for softening, de-harshing, or reducing sibilance.
apple|auhighshelffilter.name: AUHighShelfFilter

apple|auhipass.about: AUHipass is Apple's high-pass filter effect that reduces bass content below its Cutoff Frequency while passing higher frequencies. It is good for removing rumble, hum, and low-end mud from vocals, guitars, or any channel before EQ or compression. Cutoff Frequency: choose the lowest frequency you want to keep; 40-80 Hz for rumble cleanup, 80-120 Hz for voice, lower only if bass should remain, since the 6900 Hz default is too high for most cleanup. Resonance: keep near 0 dB for flat filtering, 3-8 dB for a gentle lift at the cutoff, or negative values for a duller roll-off.
apple|auhipass.name: AUHipass

apple|aulowpass.about: AULowpass is Apple’s AudioUnit low-pass filter effect that reduces frequencies above its cutoff, softening the sound and dulling the top. It is good for smoothing harsh vocals, creating distance or telephone-like effects, removing excessive brightness, and isolating low to mid material from high-end clutter. For common jobs, set Cutoff Frequency around 1000–3000 Hz for a phone or very muffled sound, 4000–6000 Hz to soften without losing much detail, and near the maximum for only light high-frequency reduction. Keep Resonance near 0 for a neutral cut, raise it to 5–15 dB to add a slight edge near the cutoff, and use 20–40 dB sparingly for a more aggressive, resonant tone.
apple|aulowpass.name: AULowpass

apple|aulowshelffilter.about: AULowShelfFilter is an Apple AudioUnit low-shelf equalizer that raises or lowers the level of frequencies below its cutoff while leaving higher frequencies mostly unchanged. It is useful for taming rumble or boom, adding warmth to voices and instruments, and making room for other low-end material. Cutoff Frequency sets where the shelf begins, ranging from 10 to 200 Hz, with 80 Hz as a safe starting point; use 30 to 60 Hz for sub rumble, 80 to 120 Hz for body, and near 200 Hz for warm low-mid presence. Gain adjusts the shelf from -40 to 40 dB, default 0; common fixes are small cuts of -3 to -10 dB for control and modest boosts of +3 to +10 dB for warmth.
apple|aulowshelffilter.name: AULowShelfFilter

apple|aumatrixreverb.about: AUMatrixReverb is Apple's algorithmic room reverb, built from a small-room and a large-room section that are blended together, with modulation and a filter on the reverb. Use it to add ambience or a sense of space to voice, instruments or a mix. Dry/Wet Mix sets the reverb amount and Small/Large Mix the balance between the two sections; Small Size and Large Size set the room sizes, Pre-Delay delays the onset of the reverb, the HiFreq Absorption controls darken each section's tail, Modulation Rate and Modulation Depth add movement, and Filter Frequency, Filter Bandwidth and Filter Gain shape the reverb's tone.
apple|aumatrixreverb.name: AUMatrixReverb

apple|aumultibandcompressor.about: AUMultibandCompressor is Apple's four-band compressor: it splits the signal at three crossover points and compresses each band separately. Use it to control boomy lows, harsh mids or sibilant highs on a mix or a dense track without compressing the whole spectrum. Crossover 1, Crossover 2 and Crossover 3 set the band split points; each band has its own Threshold, Headroom and EQ (1 to 4), Attack Time and Release Time apply to all bands, and Pre-Gain and Post-Gain set level into and out of the processor.
apple|aumultibandcompressor.name: AUMultibandCompressor

apple|aunbandeq.about: AUNBandEQ is Apple's multi-band parametric equalizer; this instance has eight bands, each with its own Bypass, Type, Frequency, Gain and Bandwidth (the per-band parameters repeat in that order), plus a Global Gain. Use it for precise tone shaping: removing rumble with a high-pass band, cutting resonances or mud, adding presence or air with shelves. A band only acts when its Bypass is off. Type selects the filter shape (in Apple's order: parametric, Butterworth low-pass, Butterworth high-pass, resonant low-pass, resonant high-pass, band-pass, band-stop, low shelf, high shelf, resonant low shelf, resonant high shelf); Bandwidth is in octaves, small for narrow cuts and larger for broad moves.
apple|aunbandeq.name: AUNBandEQ

apple|aunewpitch.about: AUNewPitch is a stereo AudioUnit pitch effect that raises or lowers pitch by up to two octaves. Use it to retune vocals or instruments, shift key, or create pitched-up or pitched-low effects while keeping the original duration. Pitch Scale is in cents: 0 no change, +/–100 one semitone, +/–1200 one octave. Smoothness default 8; raise toward 32 for smoother pitch movement, lower toward 3 for tighter but more audible processing. Spectral Coherence On keeps the tone coherent; try Off for a looser, more artificial sound. Preserve Transients On maintains attacks, useful for drums, plucks and vocals; turn Off when shifting sustained or heavily processed material.
apple|aunewpitch.name: AUNewPitch

apple|auparametriceq.about: AUParametricEQ is Apple's single-band parametric equalizer: one bell-shaped boost or cut at a chosen frequency. Use it for a single targeted fix such as cutting a resonance, boxiness or harshness, or a gentle presence boost. Center Frequency picks the frequency, Gain sets the boost or cut in dB, and Q sets the width (higher Q is narrower, for surgical cuts; low Q is broad and musical).
apple|auparametriceq.name: AUParametricEQ

apple|aupeaklimiter.about: AUPeakLimiter is Apple's peak limiter: it quickly reduces gain whenever the signal would exceed its ceiling, preventing clipping. Use it at the end of a chain to catch peaks or to raise loudness on speech or a mix. Pre-Gain drives the signal into the limiter (more pre-gain means louder output and more limiting); Attack Time and Release Time set how fast it clamps and recovers, with longer release sounding smoother and shorter release louder but more prone to distortion.
apple|aupeaklimiter.name: AUPeakLimiter

apple|aupitch.about: AUPitch is Apple's older pitch shifter: it changes pitch without changing the length of the audio. Use it to transpose a voice or instrument, or for chipmunk or deep-voice effects; it does not auto-tune. Pitch sets the amount of shift and Effect Blend mixes the shifted signal with the original; the many analysis settings (Analysis Size, Analysis Window, Overlap, Transient Follow and the threshold controls) trade smearing against artifacts and are best left at their defaults.
apple|aupitch.name: AUPitch

apple|aureverb2.about: AUReverb2 is Apple's simple algorithmic reverb, which adds a room-like tail to the signal. Use it for basic ambience on voice or instruments. Dry/Wet Mix sets how much reverb is heard; Min Delay Time and Max Delay Time set the range of the reflection delays (larger values sound like a bigger space); Low Freq Decay Time and High Freq Decay Time set how long the low and high frequencies ring, with a shorter high-frequency decay giving a darker, more natural tail; Gain sets the output level.
apple|aureverb2.name: AUReverb2

apple|aurogerbeep.about: AURogerBeep is Apple's 'roger beep' effect: it detects when speech starts and stops and adds a short radio-style beep, like a two-way radio or walkie-talkie. It is a voice-effect novelty for radio or intercom sound design. In Gate Threshold/In Gate Time and Out Gate Threshold/Out Gate Time decide when a transmission is considered to start and end, Sensitivity adjusts the detection, Roger Type chooses the beep sound, and Roger Level sets its loudness.
apple|aurogerbeep.name: AURogerBeep

apple|auroundtripaac.about: AURoundTripAAC is Apple's codec preview: it encodes the audio to AAC and decodes it again in real time, so you hear what the material will sound like after AAC compression. Use it to check how a mix or voice survives streaming or low-bitrate delivery, or to add codec artifacts deliberately. Type selects the AAC variant, Encoding Strategy the bitrate mode, and Base Bit Rate the target bitrate; lower bit rates give more audible artifacts.
apple|auroundtripaac.name: AURoundTripAAC

apple|ausampledelay.about:
AUSampleDelay is an Apple AudioUnit effect that delays the incoming stereo signal by a fixed number of samples, so the output sound follows the input with a short sample-accurate lag.

It is good for precise timing shifts, compensating plug-in latency, aligning loops, drum hits, or multi-tracked takes, and creating very short delay lines when a sample-based offset is needed.

The main parameter is In to Out Delay, ranging from 0 to 4410 samples, with default 0. Use 0 for no delay, 1 to 100 samples for subtle latency or phase alignment, and 1000 to 4410 samples for a clearly audible delay of roughly 20 to 100 milliseconds, depending on sample rate.
apple|ausampledelay.name: AUSampleDelay

apple|ausoundfieldpanner.about: AUSoundFieldPanner is one of Apple's 3D panners; it positions the input in a surround sound field (ambisonics-based) and renders it to the output channels. Use it to place a sound around the listener. Azimuth sets the horizontal angle (0 is straight ahead), Elevation the height, and Distance how far away the source is; Coordinate Scale and Reference Distance set the distance units and are normally left at their defaults; Gain sets the level.
apple|ausoundfieldpanner.name: AUSoundFieldPanner

apple|ausoundisolation.about: AUSoundIsolation is Apple's machine-learning voice isolation effect: it separates speech from background noise, music and room sound and outputs the isolated voice. Use it to clean up dialogue, podcasts or field recordings with noisy backgrounds. Wet/Dry Mix sets how much of the isolated signal is used (lower values let some of the original background back in for a more natural result); Sound to Isolate chooses what is isolated and is normally left at its default, voice.
apple|ausoundisolation.name: AUSoundIsolation

apple|ausphericalheadpanner.about: AUSphericalHeadPanner is one of Apple's 3D panners; it places the input around the listener using a spherical-head binaural model, intended for headphone listening. Use it to give a sound a direction, including behind or above the listener, in a headphone mix. Azimuth sets the horizontal angle (0 is straight ahead), Elevation the height, and Distance how far away the source sounds; Coordinate Scale and Reference Distance set the distance units and are normally left at defaults; Gain sets the level.
apple|ausphericalheadpanner.name: AUSphericalHeadPanner

apple|auvectorpanner.about: AUVectorPanner is one of Apple's 3D panners; it positions the input by amplitude (vector-based) panning across the output speakers. Use it for simple directional placement on speakers rather than binaural headphone effects. Azimuth sets the horizontal angle (0 is straight ahead), Elevation the height, and Distance how far away the source sounds; Coordinate Scale and Reference Distance set the distance units and are normally left at defaults; Gain sets the level.
apple|auvectorpanner.name: AUVectorPanner

apple|hrtfpanner.about: HRTFPanner is Apple's binaural panner: it uses head-related transfer functions to place a sound in 3D space for headphone listening. Use it to put a voice or effect to the side, behind, above or below the listener in a headphone or VR-style mix. azimuth sets the horizontal angle (0 is straight ahead), elevation the height, and distance how far away the source sounds; coordinate scale and reference distance set the distance units and are normally left at defaults; gain sets the level.
apple|hrtfpanner.name: HRTFPanner

audio ease|altiverb 8.about: Altiverb 8 is Audio Ease's convolution reverb: it places the sound in sampled real spaces (rooms, halls, churches, studios, cars and more) using impulse responses. Use it for realistic ambience on music, dialogue and post-production work, including matching a recording to a real location. Dry/Wet Mix sets the reverb amount (100 percent wet when used on a send), Reverb Time and Size scale the length and size of the space, Pre Delay separates the dry sound from the reverb, EarlyRef Gain and Tail Gain balance early reflections against the tail, the Low Damp, Mid Damp and High Damp controls shape decay per frequency range, and EQ On with EQ Bass Level and EQ Treble Level adjusts the reverb's tone. The space itself is chosen from the impulse-response browser in the plug-in's window.
audio ease|altiverb 8.name: Altiverb 8

audio ease|indoor.about: Indoor is Audio Ease's reverb for placing sound inside real recorded houses and apartments, with selectable rooms, microphone positions and speaker positions. It is aimed at post-production: making dialogue, voices or sound effects sound as if they were recorded in an ordinary indoor space, possibly in another room. Location picks the building, Microphone Position and Speaker Position set where the listener and the source are, and Doors affects how much the rooms connect; Dry/Wet and Direct On-Off control how much of the original is heard, Decay and Pre-Delay adjust the tail, Bass and Treble shape its tone, and Output Volume sets the level.
audio ease|indoor.name: Indoor

audio ease|speakerphone.about: Speakerphone is Audio Ease's speaker and telephone simulator: it makes audio sound as if it is coming from a phone, radio, TV, megaphone or small speaker, with codec, distortion, record-player and room effects. Use it for phone calls and on-screen device sound in film and podcast work, or for lo-fi treatment of music. Speaker On enables the speaker model; the EQ, Distortion, Crush (Crush Bit Depth, Crush SampleRate), Compressor, Delay and Phono sections each have an On switch and their own controls; Master DryWet Open and Master DryWet Close set the effect blend.
audio ease|speakerphone.name: Speakerphone

caelum audio|tape cassette 2.about: Tape Cassette 2 is Caelum Audio's cassette tape emulation, adding the wobble, hiss, saturation and dull top end of an old cassette. Use it to make clean recordings sound lo-fi, nostalgic or worn. Wow and Flutter set slow and fast pitch wobble, Noise sets the tape hiss level, Low Pass rolls off the highs (lower is more muffled), Saturation adds tape-style drive, and IR switches on a cassette-machine frequency response.
caelum audio|tape cassette 2.name: Tape Cassette 2

d16 group audio software|frontier.about: Frontier is D16 Group's free brick-wall limiter, which keeps peaks under a set ceiling while raising loudness. Use it on drums, buses or a full mix to catch peaks or make material louder. Threshold sets how hard the signal is limited, Release sets how quickly gain recovers, Soft Clip rounds off peaks for a smoother sound, Control Input adjusts the input level, and Output Volume sets the final level.
d16 group audio software|frontier.name: Frontier

infected mushroom|gatekeeper.about: Gatekeeper is Infected Mushroom's tempo-synced volume-shaping plug-in: drawn envelopes rhythmically gate and modulate the volume (and pan) of the signal. Use it for trance gates, rhythmic chopping, sidechain-style pumping and swells on pads, vocals or loops. - GO enables the effect and - Wet sets the blend; the envelopes are drawn in the plug-in window and stored as many numbered automation points (Auto Time, Auto Curve), which are not practical to set one by one; - Delay Time and - Delay Wet add an echo after the gate.
infected mushroom|gatekeeper.name: Gatekeeper

infected mushroom|wider.about: Wider is an Infected Mushroom stereo effect that takes a single input and increases the apparent width of the sound across its two outputs. It is useful for making drums, synths, vocals, or a full mix feel more spacious without adding reverb or changing the tone much. The main control is Amount, 0 to 100%, default 0%; start around 20–40% for subtle widening, 50–70% for an open, wide image, and use 80–100% only when the source can tolerate extreme widening. Check in mono to avoid phase problems.
infected mushroom|wider.name: Wider

izotope|insight 2.about: Insight 2 is iZotope's metering suite (loudness, true peak, spectrum, stereo image and more); it analyses the audio and does not change it. Use it to check a mix or master against loudness targets for streaming or broadcast. Its parameters, such as Integrated Loudness Value and Loudness Overflow, are read-only meter outputs rather than controls.
izotope|insight 2.name: Insight 2

izotope|izotope alloy 2.about: Alloy 2 is iZotope's mixing channel strip, combining EQ, transient shaping, an exciter, two dynamics modules, a de-esser and a limiter in one plug-in. Use it for shaping and controlling individual tracks such as vocals, drums or bass. Each module has its own gain and bypass settings; for de-essing use DE: Bypass, DE: Threshold and DE: Crossover Low Cutoff/DE: Crossover High Cutoff to set the sibilance band, and DYN1: Global Gain and DYN1: Global Mix control the first dynamics module. Global Bypass turns the whole plug-in off.
izotope|izotope alloy 2.name: iZotope Alloy 2

izotope|izotope ddly dynamic delay.about: DDLY Dynamic Delay is iZotope's delay with two delay lines switched by level: the Top delay acts on signal above the Global Threshold and the Btm (bottom) delay on signal below it. This lets loud parts get one echo treatment and quiet parts another, for example echoes only on sustained phrase ends or only on accents. Each delay has its own mode (Analog, or Grain for pitch-shifting granular repeats), Delay Time (ms) or a tempo-synced time (Host Sync Enable, Sync Delay Time), Feed Amt for feedback, HP Cutoff and LP Cutoff to filter the repeats, and Wet/Dry or Mix amounts; Intensity scales the overall effect.
izotope|izotope ddly dynamic delay.name: iZotope DDLY Dynamic Delay

izotope|izotope nectar 2.about: Nectar 2 is iZotope's all-in-one vocal processing suite, combining pitch correction, de-essing, EQ, compression, gate, saturation, delay, reverb, modulation effects and harmony in one plug-in. Use it to polish lead or backing vocals and spoken word in a single insert. Each module has its own Bypass; the main ones are PCH: (pitch correction, with PCH: Root Note, PCH: Scale and PCH: Speed), DE: (de-esser, DE: Ess Reduction and DE: Frequency), COMP: and COMP1: (compression) and DLY: (delay, DLY: Wet Mix Percent and DLY: Feedback Percent).
izotope|izotope nectar 2.name: iZotope Nectar 2

izotope|izotope nectar 2 breath control.about: Nectar 2 Breath Control is iZotope's breath remover: it detects breaths in a vocal and turns them down automatically. Use it on vocals, voice-overs and podcasts where breaths are distracting. Percent Detection Sensitivity controls how readily sounds are treated as breaths (raise it if breaths are missed, lower it if consonants get caught), Gain dB sets how much detected breaths are reduced, and Breaths Only lets you hear only what is being detected, to check the setting.
izotope|izotope nectar 2 breath control.name: iZotope Nectar 2 Breath Control

izotope|izotope trash 2.about: Trash 2 is iZotope's distortion and sound-mangling plug-in, combining filters, two-stage distortion, convolution, a dynamics module and a delay. Use it for anything from mild saturation to heavy, aggressive distortion on drums, guitars, synths or vocals. Global Mix blends the processed and original signal and GAIN: Input/Output set level into and out of the plug-in; the FILT1: section is a multi-node filter whose nodes (FILT1: Node 1 Freq, Gain, Q and Res, and so on) can be modulated by an envelope or LFO for wah and sweep effects.
izotope|izotope trash 2.name: iZotope Trash 2

izotope|nectar 4.about: Nectar 4 is iZotope's complete vocal processing suite, combining modules such as gate, EQ, compression, de-essing, pitch correction, saturation, delay, reverb and harmony in one plug-in. Use it to clean up and polish vocals or spoken word in one insert. The GATE: controls (GATE: Open, GATE: Close, GATE: Attack, GATE: Release, GATE: Ratio) remove noise between phrases, and the EQ 1: bands (EQ 1: B1 Frequency, EQ 1: B1 Gain, EQ 1: B1 Q, and so on) shape the tone; each module has its own Bypass and Wet Mix.
izotope|nectar 4.name: Nectar 4

izotope|nectar 4 auto-level.about: Nectar 4 Auto-Level is iZotope's automatic vocal leveller: it continuously rides the gain of a vocal toward a target level, like an automatic fader ride. Use it to even out a vocal or speech whose loud and quiet phrases vary, before or instead of heavy compression. ALM: Target Level sets the level to aim for, ALM: Range limits how far the gain may move, ALM: Strength sets how firmly it follows, ALM: Tame Noises keeps it from boosting noise between phrases, and ALM: Mix blends the result with the original.
izotope|nectar 4 auto-level.name: Nectar 4 Auto-Level

izotope|nectar 4 backer.about: Nectar 4 Backer is iZotope's backing-vocal generator: it creates a second, different-sounding voice from the input vocal to use as a double or backing part. Use it to thicken a lead or add a backing layer without recording another singer. BACKER: Target picks the voice character, BACKER: Pitch and BACKER: Formant shift it, BACKER: Tone adjusts its brightness, and BACKER: Blend and BACKER: Wet Mix set how much of it is heard; the PITCH: controls (PITCH: Root Note, PITCH: Scale, PITCH: Transposition) keep the generated voice in key.
izotope|nectar 4 backer.name: Nectar 4 Backer

izotope|nectar 4 breath control.about: Nectar 4 Breath Control is an iZotope vocal Fx module that detects breaths in a vocal signal and lowers them so they sit less prominently in the mix. It is useful for cleaning up close-mic'd vocals, podcast voice, or sung vocal takes where inhales or harsh breaths distract. For common jobs, set BREATH: Algorithm to Target for consistent breath-level control or Gain for simple fixed attenuation. Start BREATH: Gain around -30 dB for subtle reduction and make it more negative if breaths still stand out. Set BREATH: Sensitivity to 60, raise it if breaths are missed and lower it if normal consonants or speech are grabbed. Use BREATH: Listen to audition detection, and BREATH: Bypass to compare before and after.
izotope|nectar 4 breath control.name: Nectar 4 Breath Control

izotope|nectar 4 compressor.about: Nectar 4 Compressor is iZotope’s vocal compressor that reduces loud parts by lowering gain after a threshold, using selectable attack, release, ratio, and detection. It is good for tightening lead vocals, controlling peaks, adding glue and presence, and leveling phrases without pumping. Key parameters: COMP: Threshold set below peaks to start gain reduction; COMP: Ratio from 2 to 4 for vocals; COMP: Attack 5 ms for smooth consonants or 10-30 ms to preserve transient punch; COMP: Release 50-150 ms for steady recovery; COMP: Mode Digital or Solid-State for natural color; COMP: RMS Detection On for broader, less peaky response; COMP: Auto Gain On to compensate level; INPUT: Gain and OUTPUT: Gain to trim before and after; COMP: Wet Mix 100% for full effect, lower for parallel blend.
izotope|nectar 4 compressor.name: Nectar 4 Compressor

izotope|nectar 4 deesser.about: Nectar 4 DeEsser is an iZotope vocal de-esser that tames harsh sibilant high frequencies while leaving the rest of the tone intact. It is good for controlling "s", "t", and "ch" sounds in vocals, spoken word, and other sibilant sources. For common jobs, set DEESSER: Frequency to the offending sibilance, usually 3000–6000 Hz; use DEESSER: Threshold to control reduction amount, starting near 0 dB and lowering toward -10 dB or lower if needed. Keep DEESSER: Wet Mix at 100% for full effect or lower it for subtler taming. Use DEESSER: Listen to monitor only the affected signal, DEESSER: Bypass or GLOBAL: Bypass to A/B, and INPUT: Gain and OUTPUT: Gain to trim level; OUTPUT: Pan and Width are rarely needed unless placement changes are required.
izotope|nectar 4 deesser.name: Nectar 4 DeEsser

izotope|nectar 4 delay.about: Nectar 4 Delay is an iZotope stereo vocal delay that repeats the signal with analogue or digital/echo character, tempo-synced timing, feedback, filtering, modulation, and independent left/right settings. It is good for vocal tails, rhythmic echoes, widening a mono source, or dub-style repeats. Common settings: DELAY: Mode Analog, DELAY: Amount 30, DELAY: Wet Mix 20, DELAY: Delay L/Mono 200 ms, DELAY: Tempo Sync L/Mono On, DELAY: Tempo Beat L/Mono 1/8, DELAY: Feedback L/Mono 30, DELAY: Lowpass Freq 10000 Hz; for stereo, DELAY: Link Channels Off, DELAY: Delay R 210 ms, DELAY: Tempo Beat R 1/8, DELAY: Feedback R 30, OUTPUT: Width 20.
izotope|nectar 4 delay.name: Nectar 4 Delay

izotope|nectar 4 dimension.about: Nectar 4 Dimension is iZotope’s vocal stereo-modulation plug-in that adds a delayed, pitch-modulated copy to widen and move the sound. It is good for making lead vocals sit fuller in a mix, adding subtle sheen to pads, or creating animated chorus/phaser textures. For a gentle vocal chorus, set DIMENSION: Mode to Chorus, DIMENSION: Wet Mix around 30-50%, DIMENSION: Depth 50-80%, DIMENSION: Width 50-80%, DIMENSION: Frequency 2000-4000 Hz, and DIMENSION: Rate 0.1-0.3 Hz. For a musical pulse, turn DIMENSION: Host Sync On, set DIMENSION: Beat to 1/8 or 1/4, and keep DIMENSION: Feedback low. For phaser, use DIMENSION: Mode Phaser, DIMENSION: Frequency 500-1500 Hz, and DIMENSION: Feedback 50-80%.
izotope|nectar 4 dimension.name: Nectar 4 Dimension

izotope|nectar 4 equalizer.about: Nectar 4 Equalizer is iZotope’s 24-band EQ that shapes tone by raising or cutting frequency regions and applying dynamic level-based cuts or boosts. It is good for cleaning vocals, reducing rumble or mud, taming harshness, and adding presence or air. For low rumble, set EQ Component: B1 Shape Flat Highpass, EQ Component: B1 Frequency 40 Hz, and EQ Component: B1 Gain -3 to -6 dB. For mud, set EQ Component: B2 Frequency 600 Hz, EQ Component: B2 Gain -2 to -4 dB, and EQ Component: B2 Q 1-2. For harshness, set EQ Component: B3 Frequency 3000 Hz and EQ Component: B3 Gain -1 to -3 dB. For air, set EQ Component: B4 Shape Analog High Shelf, EQ Component: B4 Frequency 10-12 kHz, and EQ Component: B4 Gain +1 to +3 dB. Use only bands whose Enable is On and adjust EQ Component: Wet Mix as needed.
izotope|nectar 4 equalizer.name: Nectar 4 Equalizer

izotope|nectar 4 gate.about: Nectar 4 Gate is an iZotope stereo gate for vocals that lowers low-level signal once it falls below its threshold range. It is good for removing room noise between phrases, tightening takes, and keeping vocal lines clean in a mix. For common vocal jobs, set GATE: Open where you want the gate to start acting, often 20 to 30 dB below the phrase level, and set GATE: Close 3 to 8 dB for hysteresis. Use GATE: Attack 5 to 15 ms to keep phrase starts natural, GATE: Release 30 to 150 ms for quick gaps, and GATE: Ratio 15 to 30, higher for firmer control. Keep GATE: Wet Mix at 100 for a full gate. Use INPUT: Gain only to make the threshold easier to set.
izotope|nectar 4 gate.name: Nectar 4 Gate

izotope|nectar 4 pitch.about: Nectar 4 Pitch is an iZotope vocal effect that corrects sung notes to a chosen key or shifts pitch while preserving or altering formants. It is good for tuning vocal takes, matching notes to a song key, and making pitch-shifted harmonies. Key settings: set PITCH: Root Note to the song's keynote and PITCH: Scale to the song scale, or NoKey when there is no fixed key. Leave PITCH: Wet Mix at 100% for full effect. Use PITCH: Transposition in semitones for key or harmony shifts, with PITCH: Formant Shift to keep the voice natural or change its timbre, and PITCH: Formant Preservation On. PITCH: Speed at 20 ms is the default; lower it for faster, tighter correction, or raise it for smoother results. PITCH: Strength at 100% gives full correction; lower it for a more natural amount.
izotope|nectar 4 pitch.name: Nectar 4 Pitch

izotope|nectar 4 reverb.about: Nectar 4 Reverb is a stereo reverb effect for vocals that adds a processed room or space to the sound. It is good for placing lead or backing vocals in a believable space, smoothing dry recordings, and adding depth without masking the voice. Start with REVERB: Wet Mix around 20-35% for subtle space or higher for obvious room; REVERB: Pre-Delay 5-20 ms to keep words clear; REVERB: Width 80-100% for stereo spread; REVERB: Saturation 0-15% for warmth; REVERB: Low Cutoff 80-200 Hz and High Cutoff 6-12 kHz to tame mud and sizzle. Use REVERB: Mid Frequency and REVERB: Mid Gain only if the reverb needs tonal focus. Use INPUT: Gain and OUTPUT: Gain to level match, and GLOBAL: Match when the plugin offers a matched comparison.
izotope|nectar 4 reverb.name: Nectar 4 Reverb

izotope|nectar 4 saturation.about: Nectar 4 Saturation is iZotope's vocal saturation module, adding harmonic distortion for warmth, density or grit, with a high shelf to control the added brightness. Use it to help a vocal cut through a mix or to give it character. SATURATION: Mode chooses the saturation flavour, SATURATION: Amount sets how much drive is applied (low for warmth, high for obvious distortion), SATURATION: High Shelf Freq and SATURATION: High Shelf Gain tame or add top end, and SATURATION: Wet Mix blends with the dry vocal; use INPUT: Gain and OUTPUT: Gain to balance levels.
izotope|nectar 4 saturation.name: Nectar 4 Saturation

izotope|nectar 4 voices.about: Nectar 4 Voices is iZotope's vocal harmony generator: it adds up to eight pitch-shifted copies of the input vocal to build harmonies or a choir-like stack. Use it to add backing harmonies or thicken a lead. HARMONY: V1 Enable to HARMONY: V8 Enable switch voices on, HARMONY: V1 Chrom Int (chromatic) or HARMONY: V1 Maj/Min Int (scale-based) set each voice's interval, HARMONY: V1 Gain, HARMONY: V1 Pan and HARMONY: V1 Delay set its level, position and timing (likewise for V2 to V8), HARMONY: Pitch Variation and HARMONY: Time Variation add natural looseness, and HARMONY: Wet Mix sets the overall blend.
izotope|nectar 4 voices.name: Nectar 4 Voices

izotope|neoverb.about: Neoverb is iZotope's algorithmic reverb that blends three reverb engines and includes EQ before and after the reverb. Use it for vocals, instruments and mixes when you want a clean, controllable space. Dry/Wet sets the amount; R1 Gain, R2 Gain and R3 Gain balance the three engines, each with its own Time, Size and Diffusion; Predelay Time separates the dry sound from the tail; PreEQ and ReverbEQ bands (for example ReverbEQ Low Band Gain and ReverbEQ High Band Gain) shape what goes into and comes out of the reverb; Mod Rate and Mod Depth add movement.
izotope|neoverb.name: Neoverb

izotope|neutron 3.about: Neutron 3 is iZotope's mixing channel strip, combining a dynamic EQ, two multiband compressors, a gate, an exciter, a transient shaper, a Sculptor module and a limiter, plus masking analysis against other tracks. Use it for shaping and controlling individual tracks or buses during mixing. Global Input Gain and Global Output Gain set levels and Width adjusts stereo width; the first compressor is set per band with C1 B1 Threshold, C1 B1 Ratio, C1 B1 Attack and C1 B1 Release (B2, B3 for the other bands), and SC Amount with SC Target controls the Sculptor.
izotope|neutron 3.name: Neutron 3

izotope|neutron 3 compressor.about: Neutron 3 Compressor is an iZotope stereo dynamics effect that compresses level variations and can use Unmask to open up masked passages. It suits vocals, drums, bass, and mix bus work for taming peaks, adding consistency, or making elements sit better. For common jobs, set C1 B1 Threshold, C1 B1 Ratio, C1 B1 Attack, C1 B1 Release, C1 B1 Knee, and C1 B1 Mix; typical settings are threshold at first gain reduction, ratio 2-4:1, attack 5-30 ms, release 50-300 ms, knee 0-20, mix 100%. Keep C1 Level Detection Method RMS, C1 Auto Gain On, and C1 Auto Release Off. For tonal shaping, use C1 B2 Threshold, C1 B2 Ratio, C1 B3 Threshold, and C1 B3 Ratio. Balance with Global Input Gain, Global Output Gain, and C1 Global Gain. Use Unmask Amount only when clarity needs help, trying 50-100%.
izotope|neutron 3 compressor.name: Neutron 3 Compressor

izotope|neutron 3 equalizer.about: Neutron 3 Equalizer is iZotope's twelve-band EQ in which any band can also be made dynamic, cutting or boosting only when the signal crosses a threshold. Use it for tonal shaping and for taming resonances or harshness that come and go. Each band has EQ B1 Frequency, EQ B1 Gain, EQ B1 Q and EQ B1 Shape (and so on to B12); EQ B1 Threshold to EQ B12 Threshold set when a dynamic band reacts. Global Input Gain and Global Output Gain set levels.
izotope|neutron 3 equalizer.name: Neutron 3 Equalizer

izotope|neutron 3 exciter.about: Neutron 3 Exciter is iZotope's multiband harmonic exciter: it adds saturation-style harmonics to make a sound brighter, warmer or more present. Use it on dull vocals, guitars, synths, drums or buses. Up to three bands each have EXC B1 Drive and EXC B1 Blend (B2, B3 likewise), with EXC B1 X and EXC B1 Y choosing the saturation character on the plug-in's pad; EXC Post Filter Freq and EXC Post Filter Gain shape the top end afterwards, and EXC Global Mix blends the result with the dry signal.
izotope|neutron 3 exciter.name: Neutron 3 Exciter

izotope|neutron 3 gate.about: Neutron 3 Gate is an iZotope gate that mutes or reduces low-level sound using threshold, timing, ratio, and side-chain filtering. It is good for removing hum, hiss, bleed, and room noise, tightening drums and percussion, and controlling tails while preserving wanted transients. Start with G1 B1 Bypass Off, G1 B1 Open at -40 to -60 dB, G1 B1 Close at 0 to 15 dB, G1 B1 Attack 0.1 to 5 ms, G1 B1 Release 80 to 300 ms, G1 B1 Ratio 10 to 30:1 for hard gating or 2 to 5:1 for ducking, G1 B1 Hold 0 to 0.1 s, and G1 Global Mix 100. Set G1 B2 Bypass Off and G1 B3 Bypass Off, then match their Open, Close, Attack, Release, Ratio, and Hold. Use G1 SC Filter HP Freq 100-200 Hz and G1 SC Filter LP Freq 2-6 kHz.
izotope|neutron 3 gate.name: Neutron 3 Gate

izotope|neutron 3 sculptor.about: Neutron 3 Sculptor is iZotope's adaptive tone-matching module: it continuously adjusts the spectrum of a track toward a target profile for the chosen instrument type. Use it for quick tonal balancing of a track during mixing. SC Target selects the profile, SC Amount sets how strongly it is applied, SC Speed how fast it reacts, SC Tone tilts the result, and SC Action Region Low Freq and SC Action Region High Freq limit it to a frequency range; SC Global Mix blends with the original.
izotope|neutron 3 sculptor.name: Neutron 3 Sculptor

izotope|neutron 3 transient shaper.about: Neutron 3 Transient Shaper is iZotope's multiband transient shaper: it boosts or reduces the attack and sustain of a sound separately in up to three frequency bands. Use it to add punch or soften hits on drums and percussion, or to shorten or lengthen ringing tails. TS B1 Attack and TS B1 Sustain (B2, B3 likewise) set the amounts, with positive values emphasising and negative values reducing; TS B1 Contour sets the shape of the response, TS Global Mode the detection behaviour, and TS Global Mix blends with the original.
izotope|neutron 3 transient shaper.name: Neutron 3 Transient Shaper

izotope|neutron 4.about: Neutron 4 is iZotope's mixing channel strip, combining a dynamic EQ, multiband compressors, a gate, an exciter, a transient shaper, Sculptor, Unmask and a limiter, plus a Mix Assistant. Use it for shaping and controlling individual tracks or buses during mixing. Global Input Gain and Global Output Gain set levels and Width adjusts stereo width; the first compressor is set per band with C1 B1 Threshold, C1 B1 Ratio, C1 B1 Attack and C1 B1 Release (B2, B3 for the other bands), and SC Amount with SC Target controls the Sculptor.
izotope|neutron 4.name: Neutron 4

izotope|neutron 4 compressor.about: Neutron 4 Compressor is iZotope's compressor module, usable as a single-band or up to three-band compressor, with optional Punch mode for added transient impact. Use it to control the dynamics of vocals, drums, bass or buses. Per band, C1 B1 Threshold, C1 B1 Ratio, C1 B1 Attack, C1 B1 Release, C1 B1 Knee and C1 B1 Mix (and the same for B2, B3) set the compression; C1 Level Detection Method chooses peak or RMS behaviour and C1 Auto Gain compensates level; C1 B1 Punch Amount adds punch; Global Output Gain sets the final level.
izotope|neutron 4 compressor.name: Neutron 4 Compressor

izotope|neutron 4 equalizer.about: Neutron 4 Equalizer is iZotope's twelve-band EQ in which any band can also be made dynamic, cutting or boosting only when the signal crosses a threshold. Use it for tonal shaping and for taming resonances or harshness that come and go. Each band has EQ B1 Frequency, EQ B1 Gain, EQ B1 Q and EQ B1 Shape (and so on to B12); EQ B1 Threshold to EQ B12 Threshold set when a dynamic band reacts. Global Input Gain and Global Output Gain set levels.
izotope|neutron 4 equalizer.name: Neutron 4 Equalizer

izotope|neutron 4 exciter.about: Neutron 4 Exciter is iZotope's multiband harmonic exciter: it adds saturation-style harmonics to make a sound brighter, warmer or more present. Use it on dull vocals, guitars, synths, drums or buses. Up to three bands each have EXC B1 Drive and EXC B1 Blend (B2, B3 likewise), with EXC B1 X and EXC B1 Y choosing the saturation character and EXC B1 Trash Mode adding heavier distortion; EXC Tone and EXC Tame adjust brightness and harshness, EXC Post Filter Freq and EXC Post Filter Gain shape the top end, and EXC Global Mix blends with the dry signal.
izotope|neutron 4 exciter.name: Neutron 4 Exciter

izotope|neutron 4 gate.about: iZotope Neutron 4 Gate is a stereo dynamics gate that suppresses quiet passages, using band-specific gate controls and sidechain filtering. It is good for removing noise, bleed, and unwanted low-level audio from drums, vocals, or mixes while keeping wanted transients. Set G1 B1 Open and G1 B1 Close to separate wanted events from noise, starting from Open -80 dB and Close 0 dB and adjusting until the gate opens only when needed. Use G1 B1 Attack 1 ms for tight drums or 5-10 ms for vocals, G1 B1 Release 80-200 ms, and G1 B1 Hold 0-0.1 s to stop chattering. Adjust G1 SC Filter HP Freq to 40-120 Hz and G1 SC Filter LP Freq to 18000 Hz for full-band or lower to 2000 Hz for a focused trigger. Leave G1 Global Mix at 100 and Nectar Unmask Bypass on unless using that feature.
izotope|neutron 4 gate.name: Neutron 4 Gate

izotope|neutron 4 sculptor.about: Neutron 4 Sculptor is iZotope's adaptive tone-matching module: it continuously adjusts the spectrum of a track toward a target profile for the chosen instrument type. Use it for quick tonal balancing of a track during mixing. SC Target selects the profile, SC Amount sets how strongly it is applied, SC Speed how fast it reacts, SC Tone tilts the result, and SC Action Region Low Freq and SC Action Region High Freq limit it to a frequency range; SC Global Mix blends with the original.
izotope|neutron 4 sculptor.name: Neutron 4 Sculptor

izotope|neutron 4 transient shaper.about: Neutron 4 Transient Shaper is iZotope's multiband transient shaper: it boosts or reduces the attack and sustain of a sound separately in up to three frequency bands. Use it to add punch or soften hits on drums and percussion, or to shorten or lengthen ringing tails. TS B1 Attack and TS B1 Sustain (B2, B3 likewise) set the amounts, with positive values emphasising and negative values reducing; TS B1 Contour sets the shape of the response, TS Global Mode the detection behaviour, and TS Global Mix blends with the original.
izotope|neutron 4 transient shaper.name: Neutron 4 Transient Shaper

izotope|neutron 4 unmask.about: Neutron 4 Unmask is iZotope's masking-reduction module: it dynamically cuts frequencies in the track it is on wherever they clash with a sidechain track, so the other track (usually a vocal) comes through more clearly. Use it on music beds or instruments that compete with a vocal or dialogue. It needs a sidechain source to compare against; Unmask Amount sets how much is cut, Unmask Sensitivity how readily it reacts, Unmask Attack and Unmask Release its speed, Unmask Action Region Low Freq and Unmask Action Region High Freq limit the frequency range, and Unmask Global Mix blends with the original.
izotope|neutron 4 unmask.name: Neutron 4 Unmask

izotope|ozone 10.about: Ozone 10 is iZotope's mastering suite, combining modules such as EQ, dynamic EQ, dynamics, imager, exciter, vintage processors and the Maximizer limiter in one plug-in. Use it to master a finished mix: tonal balance, stereo width, dynamics and final loudness. Each module has its own bypass; the EQ is set per band with EQ: St/M/L Frequency 1, EQ: St/M/L Gain 1, EQ: St/M/L Q 1, EQ: St/M/L Shape 1 and EQ: St/M/L Enable 1 (through 8), and EQ: S/R bands do the same for the side channel in mid/side mode.
izotope|ozone 10.name: Ozone 10

izotope|ozone 11.about: Ozone 11 is iZotope's mastering suite, combining modules such as EQ, dynamic EQ, dynamics, imager, exciter, clarity, stabilizer and the Maximizer limiter in one plug-in. Use it to master a finished mix: tonal balance, stereo width, dynamics and final loudness. Each module has its own bypass (EQ: Bypass for the EQ); the EQ is set per band with EQ: Stereo/Main Frequency 1, EQ: Stereo/Main Gain 1, EQ: Stereo/Main Q 1, EQ: Stereo/Main Shape 1 and EQ: Stereo/Main Enable 1 (through 8), EQ: Global Amount scales the EQ curve, and EQ: Aux bands work on the second channel in mid/side or left/right mode.
izotope|ozone 11.name: Ozone 11

izotope|ozone 9.about: Ozone 9 is iZotope's mastering suite, combining modules such as EQ, dynamic EQ, dynamics, imager, exciter, vintage processors, low-end focus and the Maximizer limiter in one plug-in. Use it to master a finished mix: tonal balance, stereo width, dynamics and final loudness. Each module has its own bypass; the EQ is set per band with EQ: St/M/L Frequency 1, EQ: St/M/L Gain 1, EQ: St/M/L Q 1, EQ: St/M/L Shape 1 and EQ: St/M/L Enable 1 (through 8), and EQ: S/R bands do the same for the side channel in mid/side mode.
izotope|ozone 9.name: Ozone 9

izotope|ozone 9 dynamic eq.about: iZotope Ozone 9 Dynamic EQ is a multiband dynamic equaliser that cuts or boosts a frequency range only when the audio crosses a threshold. It is good for taming bass plosives, boxy midrange, resonant peaks, harsh vocals, and keeping a loud mix or master balanced without constant static EQ. For most jobs set DYNEQ: St/M/L Frequency 1 to 80-120 Hz for bass control or 300-800 Hz for boxiness, then use DYNEQ: St/M/L Gain 1 around -4 to -10 dB, DYNEQ: St/M/L Q 1 at 1-4, DYNEQ: St/M/L Threshold 1 near -30 to -20 dB, DYNEQ: St/M/L Attack 1 at 2-20 ms, DYNEQ: St/M/L Release 1 at 80-120 ms, and DYNEQ: St/M/L Shape 1 as Bell or Proportional Q.
izotope|ozone 9 dynamic eq.name: Ozone 9 Dynamic EQ

izotope|ozone 9 dynamics.about: Ozone 9 Dynamics is iZotope's multiband dynamics module with up to four bands, each with its own compressor and limiter. Use it on a master or bus to control peaks and level differences in specific frequency ranges, or to add glue. For each band, DYN: Band 1 Comp Threshold, DYN: Band 1 Comp Ratio, DYN: Band 1 Comp Attack and DYN: Band 1 Comp Release set compression and DYN: Band 1 Lim Threshold sets the limiter (and likewise for Bands 2 to 4); DYN: Band 1 Gain and DYN: Band 1 Mix set band level and blend, DYN: Global Mix blends the whole module, and DYN: Level Detection Method chooses peak or RMS-style detection.
izotope|ozone 9 dynamics.name: Ozone 9 Dynamics

izotope|ozone 9 equalizer.about: Ozone 9 Equalizer is iZotope's eight-band parametric EQ from the Ozone 9 mastering suite, with stereo, mid/side or left/right processing. It is used for broad tonal balance on mixes and masters: removing rumble with a high-pass, cutting mud or boxiness, adding presence or air, or treating the side channel separately. Each band has EQ: St/M/L Frequency, Gain, Q, Shape and Enable controls (bands 1-8), and the EQ: S/R parameters are the matching bank for the side or right channel. Keep mastering moves small and use GAIN: Output L (Locked) to match level when comparing.
izotope|ozone 9 equalizer.name: Ozone 9 Equalizer

izotope|ozone 9 exciter.about: Ozone 9 Exciter is iZotope's multiband harmonic exciter, which adds saturation-generated harmonics to make material brighter, warmer or more present. It is used on masters, buses, vocals and synths to add sparkle or density without plain EQ boosts, and in mid/side mode to add excitement to the sides only. EXC: Mode picks the saturation character (tube, tape and similar models), the St/M Band 1-4 Amount and Mix parameters set how much is added per band, EXC: Link Bands moves the bands together, and EXC: Mid/Side Mode enables separate EXC: Side Band controls. Small amounts go a long way; check level with the output gain.
izotope|ozone 9 exciter.name: Ozone 9 Exciter

izotope|ozone 9 imager.about: Ozone 9 Imager is iZotope's four-band stereo width processor, which narrows or widens the stereo image separately in each frequency band. It is used to keep low frequencies mono and centered, widen upper mids and highs, and check mono compatibility of a mix. IMG: Band 1 Width Percent through IMG: Band 4 Width Percent set width per band (negative narrows, positive widens), IMG: Link Bands moves them together, and IMG: Enable Stereoize with IMG: Stereoizer Delay can create width from near-mono material. Widening the low band is rarely a good idea.
izotope|ozone 9 imager.name: Ozone 9 Imager

izotope|ozone 9 low end focus.about: Ozone 9 Low End Focus is iZotope's low-frequency contrast tool, which makes the bass region punchier or smoother within a chosen frequency range. It is used on masters and mixes to tighten or soften kick and bass without conventional EQ or compression. LEF: St/Mid Mode chooses Punchy or Smooth, LEF: St/Mid Contrast sets how strongly the effect acts, LEF: St/Mid Action Region Low and High set the frequency range, and LEF: St/Mid Gain makes up level; the LEF: Side controls do the same for the side channel.
izotope|ozone 9 low end focus.name: Ozone 9 Low End Focus

izotope|ozone 9 master rebalance.about: Ozone 9 Master Rebalance is iZotope's source-separation tool that raises or lowers one element of a finished stereo mix, such as vocals, bass or drums, without stems. It is used to fix a mix where the vocal or the rhythm section sits too loud or too quiet. The target element is chosen in the plug-in interface; MRB: Gain sets how much that element is boosted or cut, and small moves sound most natural.
izotope|ozone 9 master rebalance.name: Ozone 9 Master Rebalance

izotope|ozone 9 maximizer.about: Ozone 9 Maximizer is iZotope's mastering limiter, which raises loudness while holding peaks under a set ceiling. It is the last stage of a mastering chain for reaching a target loudness and preventing clipping or inter-sample peaks. Lower MAX: Threshold to push level, set MAX: Ceiling for the output peak limit, and turn on MAX: True Peak Limiting for distribution masters. MAX: Mode selects the IRC algorithm (with MAX: IRC III Style and MAX: IRC IV Style refining it), MAX: Character trades speed against smoothness, and MAX: Enable Transient Shaping with MAX: Transient Shaping Amt helps keep punch.
izotope|ozone 9 maximizer.name: Ozone 9 Maximizer

izotope|ozone 9 spectral shaper.about: Ozone 9 Spectral Shaper is iZotope's spectral compressor, which smooths harsh or resonant frequencies within a chosen range by compressing the loudest parts of the spectrum. It is used to tame harshness, sibilant edge or ringing resonances on masters and buses more transparently than a static EQ cut. SPSHPR: St/Mid Threshold sets how much is caught, SPSHPR: St/Mid Action Region Low and High set the frequency range, SPSHPR: St/Mid Attack and Release set timing, and SPSHPR: St/Mid Tone tilts where the processing focuses; the SPSHPR: Side controls treat the side channel separately.
izotope|ozone 9 spectral shaper.name: Ozone 9 Spectral Shaper

izotope|ozone 9 vintage compressor.about: Ozone 9 Vintage Compressor is iZotope's analog-style compressor with stereo or mid/side operation, for adding glue, punch and warmth. It is used on mix buses and masters, and on drums, bass or vocals. The main controls are VCOMP: St/Mid Threshold, VCOMP: St/Mid Ratio, VCOMP: St/Mid Attack and VCOMP: St/Mid Release, with VCOMP: St/Mid Mode choosing Balanced, Sharp or Smooth character and VCOMP: St/Mid Auto Gain compensating level. The Det. Filt. parameters shape what the detector hears (for example a high-pass so bass does not drive the compression), and the VCOMP: Side controls compress the side channel separately.
izotope|ozone 9 vintage compressor.name: Ozone 9 Vintage Compressor

izotope|ozone 9 vintage eq.about: Ozone 9 Vintage EQ is iZotope's emulation of a passive tube equalizer in the style of the Pultec program and mid-range EQs. It is used for broad, musical tone shaping on masters and buses: low-end weight, warmth, presence and air rather than surgical cuts. VEQ: St/M/L Low Frequency with Low Boost Amount and Low Cut Amount shapes the bottom (boosting and cutting together gives the classic tightened low end), High Boost Frequency, High Boost Amount and High Q add top, High Cut Amount softens highs, and the Low-Mid, Mid and High-Mid controls shape the midrange. The VEQ: S/R parameters are the matching bank for the side or right channel.
izotope|ozone 9 vintage eq.name: Ozone 9 Vintage EQ

izotope|ozone 9 vintage limiter.about: Ozone 9 Vintage Limiter is iZotope's analog-style peak limiter, modeled on classic tube limiting, for raising loudness with a warmer, softer character than a clean digital limiter. It is used on masters and buses when some color and glue is wanted. Lower VLM: Threshold to push level into the limiter, set VLM: Ceiling for the maximum output, choose the character with VLM: Tube Type and VLM: Character, and enable VLM: True Peak Limiting for distribution masters.
izotope|ozone 9 vintage limiter.name: Ozone 9 Vintage Limiter

izotope|ozone 9 vintage tape.about: Ozone 9 Vintage Tape is iZotope's tape machine emulation, adding saturation, soft compression and tape-style frequency response. It is used to warm and glue mixes, masters, drums or vocals and to take the edge off digital highs. VTAPE: Input Drive sets how hard the tape is hit, VTAPE: Speed changes the tape speed and with it the low-end and high-end response, VTAPE: Bias and VTAPE: Harmonics shape the saturation, and VTAPE: Low Emphasis and VTAPE: High Emphasis adjust the low and high balance. Trim the output to compare at matched level.
izotope|ozone 9 vintage tape.name: Ozone 9 Vintage Tape

izotope|relay.about: Relay is iZotope's channel utility plug-in for gain, pan, stereo width, phase and channel delay, with a high-pass filter. It is used for basic clean-up and level or image fixes on a track: trimming level, narrowing or summing to mono, inverting phase, nudging timing between channels, and removing low-frequency rumble. Key parameters are Global Output Gain, Pan, Width, Sum to Mono, Invert Phase, Delay (L) and Delay (R), and Enable HPF with HPF Cutoff Frequency and HPF Slope. It also links with iZotope's Neutron and Nectar (Visual Mixer, Unmask); the Nectar Unmask parameters only matter when used with Nectar.
izotope|relay.name: Relay

izotope|rx 10 breath control.about: RX 10 Breath Control is an iZotope restoration effect that finds breaths in stereo audio and reduces them without removing the speech itself. It is useful for vocals, dialogue, podcasts, narration, and any close-mic recording where breathing is audible but distracting. For common cleanup, set Algorithm to Target and Sensitivity to 60.00; raise Sensitivity if quiet breaths are missed, lower it if it reaches consonants or words. Use Gain around -30.00 dB for moderate control, lower it for stronger reduction, and move it toward 0.00 for a subtler effect. If a fixed attenuation is preferred, set Algorithm to Gain. Keep Global bypass Off while using the plug-in and On only to mute it.
izotope|rx 10 breath control.name: RX 10 Breath Control

izotope|rx 10 de-click.about: iZotope RX 10 De-click is a stereo restoration effect that removes clicks, ticks, and other short impulsive noises from the audio. It is good for cleaning speech, vinyl, cymbals, percussion, or any sparse clicks where you want to keep transients intact. Start with Algorithm Single-band, and use Low-latency only when timing matters. Set Sensitivity around 3.00, raise it to 5.00–8.00 if clicks remain, and lower it if musical detail is lost. Turn Output clicks only On to inspect what is being detected. Keep Frequency skew at 0.00 unless one region of the spectrum needs emphasis, then use a small value toward the offending range. Use Click widening 0.00 first; raise it slightly, perhaps 0.5–2.0, when narrow clicks are missed.
izotope|rx 10 de-click.name: RX 10 De-click

izotope|rx 10 de-clip.about: RX 10 De-clip is an iZotope restoration effect that removes digital clipping by reconstructing flat peaks so the sound sounds less distorted and more natural. It is good for salvaging overdriven vocal, drum, or full-mix recordings, especially when a few harsh peaks are the only damage. Set Clipping threshold to where the flat tops begin, usually around -1 dB, and use Positive threshold or Negative threshold separately only if clipping is one-sided; turn Enable Asymmetric On in that case. Use Quality High for careful work and Low for quick passes. Keep Input Gain at 0 dB unless the file needs level adjustment, then use Makeup gain to bring the result up slightly, and leave Post-limiter On to keep reconstructed peaks from re-clipping.
izotope|rx 10 de-clip.name: RX 10 De-clip

izotope|rx 10 de-crackle.about: RX 10 De-crackle is an iZotope restoration plug-in that reduces crackle, clicks, and pops in stereo audio by detecting and removing transient noise artifacts. It is good for old vinyl, tape, spoken word, music, and damaged recordings where unwanted surface noise should be cleaned without over-processing the wanted signal. For common jobs, set Quality to Low for quick cleanup and High for careful material. Start Strength at 5.00, increase to 6.00 to 8.00 for heavy crackle, and lower to 1.00 to 3.00 for faint noise. Keep Amplitude skew at 0.00 unless removal is too aggressive or leaves too much crackle, then nudge it slightly. Use Output crackle only On to isolate removed artifacts for reference, and Global bypass to compare before and after.
izotope|rx 10 de-crackle.name: RX 10 De-crackle

izotope|rx 10 de-ess.about: RX 10 De-ess is iZotope's de-esser, which reduces harsh sibilance (s, sh, t sounds) in voice recordings. It is used on dialogue, podcasts, voice-over and sung vocals. Threshold sets how much sibilance is caught, Cutoff freq sets the lower edge of the sibilant range, and Algorithm chooses Classic (broadband reduction above the cutoff) or Spectral (reduces only the sibilant frequencies, shaped by Spectral shaping and Spectral tilt). Speed sets how quickly it reacts, and Output ess only lets you hear what is being removed.
izotope|rx 10 de-ess.name: RX 10 De-ess

izotope|rx 10 de-hum.about: RX 10 De-hum is iZotope's hum remover, which notches out mains hum (50 or 60 Hz) and its harmonics. It is used on dialogue, instruments and field recordings with electrical hum or buzz. Base frequency sets the hum fundamental (Enable learning can detect it, Enable adaptive learning follows drifting hum), Number of harmonics and the Harmonic 1-8 gain parameters control how far up the harmonic series it cuts, and Filter Q sets how narrow the notches are. Enable highpass and Enable lowpass add extra filtering, and Output hum only lets you hear what is removed.
izotope|rx 10 de-hum.name: RX 10 De-hum

izotope|rx 10 de-plosive.about: iZotope RX 10 De-plosive is a restoration effect that detects plosive bursts and reduces their low-frequency energy. It is good for cleaning close-miked dialogue, narration, vocals, podcasts, and voice-over where hard P, B, or T consonants cause popping. Start near defaults: Sensitivity 5.00, Strength 5.00, and Frequency limit [Hz] 200.00. For transparent speech, keep Strength 3.00-5.00 and Frequency limit [Hz] 150.00-250.00; raise Sensitivity 6.00-8.00 and Strength 6.00-10.00 for missed or strong pops. Raise Frequency limit [Hz] toward 300.00-500.00 only if low-end plops remain. Use Global bypass to compare the effect off.
izotope|rx 10 de-plosive.name: RX 10 De-plosive

izotope|rx 10 de-reverb.about: RX 10 De-reverb is iZotope's reverb reduction tool, which reduces room reflections and reverb tails to make a recording drier. It is used on dialogue, voice-over and instrument takes recorded in reflective rooms. Reduction sets how much reverb is removed, Tail length should roughly match the room's decay, and Artifact smoothing reduces watery processing artifacts. Band strength low, low-mid, high-mid and high set how strongly reverb is reduced in each frequency region, and Output reverb only lets you hear what is being removed. Heavy settings can make speech sound thin or processed.
izotope|rx 10 de-reverb.name: RX 10 De-reverb

izotope|rx 10 guitar de-noise.about: RX 10 Guitar De-noise is an iZotope restoration effect that reduces squeaks, pick noise, and amplifier-related noise in electric guitar recordings while trying to preserve the performance. It is good for cleaning guitar takes, removing finger squeak, pick scratches, and amp or room noise. Start with SQUEAK: Bypass Off, SQUEAK: Sensitivity 3.00, SQUEAK: Reduction 4.00 for light squeak cleanup; raise sensitivity for obvious squeaks. For pick noise, set PICK: Bypass Off, PICK: Sensitivity 5.00, PICK: Attack 1.00, PICK: Reduction 5.00, and lower attack if picks are too clipped. For amp noise, set AMP: Bypass Off, AMP: Resolution 128, AMP: Sensitivity 5.00; higher resolution may help tonal amp artifacts.
izotope|rx 10 guitar de-noise.name: RX 10 Guitar De-noise

izotope|rx 10 mouth de-click.about: RX 10 Mouth De-click is iZotope's tool for removing mouth noises (lip smacks, tongue and saliva clicks) from voice recordings. It is used on voice-over, narration, podcasts and close-miked vocals. Sensitivity sets how readily clicks are detected (too high can dull consonants), Frequency skew biases detection toward lower or higher clicks, and Output clicks only lets you hear what is being removed.
izotope|rx 10 mouth de-click.name: RX 10 Mouth De-click

izotope|rx 10 repair assistant.about: RX 10 Repair Assistant is iZotope's one-stop repair plug-in that analyzes audio and applies a chain of RX modules (de-clip, de-click, de-hum, de-noise, de-reverb, de-ess and tone) at once. It is used for quick clean-up of dialogue, podcasts and sound effects when there is no time for module-by-module work. Source mode tells it what kind of material it is processing, each module can be switched off with its bypass parameter (for example De-noise bypass), and the matching amount parameters (De-noise amount, De-reverb amount and so on) set how strongly each repair is applied.
izotope|rx 10 repair assistant.name: RX 10 Repair Assistant

izotope|rx 10 spectral de-noise.about: RX 10 Spectral De-noise is iZotope's broadband noise reduction, which learns or adapts to a noise profile and removes steady background noise such as hiss, air conditioning or room tone. It is used on dialogue, music and field recordings with constant noise; for electrical hum, De-hum is the better tool. Noise reduction (dB) sets how much noise is removed and Noise threshold (dB) how much of the signal is treated as noise, with separate Tonal threshold and Tonal reduction controls for tonal noise. Adaptive learning follows changing noise, Quality trades CPU for fewer artifacts, Artifact control limits watery artifacts, and Output noise only lets you hear what is removed.
izotope|rx 10 spectral de-noise.name: RX 10 Spectral De-noise

izotope|rx 10 voice de-noise.about: RX 10 Voice De-noise is iZotope's adaptive noise reduction tuned for speech, removing steady background noise while keeping voices natural. It is used on dialogue, podcasts and voice-over with hiss, fan or room noise. Reduction sets the amount of noise removed, Adaptive Mode lets it follow changing noise, Optimize for chooses dialogue or music material, and Filter type trades a gentler sound against stronger, more surgical reduction. Master threshold and Threshold 1-6 set the noise floor overall and per band.
izotope|rx 10 voice de-noise.name: RX 10 Voice De-noise

izotope|trash.about: Trash is iZotope's multiband distortion and sound-mangling plug-in, combining distortion, filters, convolution (cabinet, speaker and space impulses) and dynamics across several frequency bands. It is used for anything from subtle saturation to heavily destroyed drums, bass, synths and vocals. Low Mid Cutoff splits the bands, and each band has its own distortion (B1 Trash Drive, B1 Trash Mix, B1 Trash Output Gain, blend and style controls) and convolution (B1 Convolution Enabled, B1 Convolution Mix) settings, with matching B2 controls for the next band. The global Filter Cutoff, Global Mix and Global Output Gain, with Auto Gain Enabled and Limiter Enabled, keep the result usable.
izotope|trash.name: Trash

izotope|vinyl.about: Vinyl is iZotope's free lo-fi plug-in that simulates the sound of vinyl records: surface noise, dust and scratches, wear, record warp and the frequency response of records from a chosen era. It is used to make samples, beats, vocals or whole mixes sound old or record-like. Year sets the era-dependent tone, Wear dulls and degrades the sound, Dust Amount and Dust Gain add crackle, Scratch Amount and Scratch Gain add scratches, Mech Noise and Elec Noise add turntable noise, and Warp Depth with Warp Model adds pitch wobble. Spin Down creates a turntable stop, and Mono and Lo-fi add further degradation.
izotope|vinyl.name: Vinyl

izotope|vocal doubler.about: Vocal Doubler is iZotope's free doubling plug-in that adds subtle, varied copies of a vocal to simulate a double-tracked performance. It is used to thicken and widen lead or backing vocals without recording a second take. Amount sets how much doubled signal is heard, Separation sets how far apart the doubles spread in the stereo field, and Variation sets how much the doubles drift in timing and pitch. Effect-Only outputs only the doubles, for use in parallel.
izotope|vocal doubler.name: Vocal Doubler

izotope|vocalsynth 2.about: VocalSynth 2 is iZotope's vocal effects processor that turns a voice into synthetic and robotic textures with five combinable engines: Biovox, Vocoder, Talkbox, Compuvox and Polyvox. It is used for vocoder and talkbox sounds, robotic or computer voices, and harmonized synthetic vocal layers in electronic, pop and hip-hop production. Turn on an engine with its Enable parameter (BVX: Enable, VCDR: Enable and so on) and set its level with its Lvl parameter; Output: Mix blends with the dry voice and Gate: Threshold keeps background noise from triggering the engines. VCDR: Mode chooses the vocoder character, and the BVX: Vowel X and BVX: Vowel Y controls shape Biovox's vowel formants.
izotope|vocalsynth 2.name: VocalSynth 2

kilohearts|khs 3-band eq.about: kHs 3-Band EQ is a Kilohearts three-band equaliser that separates the sound into low, mid, and high bands and lets you raise or lower each band. It is good for quick tonal balance, removing boom or muddiness, and adding clarity. Use Low Split to choose where the low band ends, 25 Hz to 600 Hz, default 220 Hz; use High Split to choose where highs start, 700 Hz to 15.0 kHz, default 2.20 kHz. For bass level, adjust Low from -16 to +16 dB; for body, adjust Mid; for presence or air, adjust High. Start with 0 dB and make small cuts or boosts of a few dB. Bypass compares with the effect off.
kilohearts|khs 3-band eq.name: kHs 3-Band EQ

kilohearts|khs bitcrush.about: kHs Bitcrush is Kilohearts' bitcrusher, which reduces sample rate and bit depth for gritty, lo-fi digital distortion. It is used for 8-bit and chiptune textures, crunchy drums and degraded synths or vocals. Rate sets the reduced sample rate (lower is more aliased), Bits sets the bit depth (lower is noisier and harsher), ADC Quality and DAC Quality control how clean the conversion filtering is, Dither smooths quantization, and Mix blends with the dry signal.
kilohearts|khs bitcrush.name: kHs Bitcrush

kilohearts|khs chorus.about: kHs Chorus is Kilohearts' chorus effect, which adds modulated delayed copies of the signal for thickness and stereo width. It is used on synths, pads, guitars and vocals. Delay sets the base delay time, Rate and Depth set the speed and amount of modulation, Taps sets the number of delayed voices, Spread sets stereo width, and Mix blends with the dry signal; lower Mix and Depth give a subtler result.
kilohearts|khs chorus.name: kHs Chorus

kilohearts|khs comb filter.about: kHs Comb Filter is Kilohearts' comb filter, which mixes the signal with a very short delayed copy to create a series of evenly spaced peaks and notches. It is used for metallic, hollow or pitched resonant tones in sound design and for flanger-like effects when its frequency is modulated. Cutoff sets the comb frequency (the spacing of the peaks), Polarity switches between positive and negative feedback for different peak/notch patterns, Stereo offsets the two channels, and Mix blends with the dry signal.
kilohearts|khs comb filter.name: kHs Comb Filter

kilohearts|khs compressor.about: kHs Compressor is Kilohearts' simple compressor, which reduces the level of loud passages to even out dynamics, with an optional sidechain input. It is used for leveling vocals, adding punch to drums or bass, light bus glue and sidechain ducking. Threshold and Ratio set how much compression is applied, Attack and Release set its timing, Mode chooses the detection behavior, and Makeup restores level afterwards.
kilohearts|khs compressor.name: kHs Compressor

kilohearts|khs delay.about: kHs Delay is Kilohearts' delay effect, producing repeats in milliseconds or synced to tempo, with feedback, ping-pong and ducking. It is used for echoes, slapback and rhythmic repeats on vocals, synths, guitars and drums. Sync Mode chooses free time (Delay Time (ms)) or tempo sync (Delay Time (steps) with Delay Denominator), Feedback sets how many repeats there are, Ping-Pong bounces repeats between left and right, Duck lowers the echoes while the input is playing so they do not clutter the dry signal, and Mix blends wet and dry.
kilohearts|khs delay.name: kHs Delay

kilohearts|khs distortion.about: kHs Distortion is Kilohearts' waveshaping distortion with several distortion types, for anything from warm saturation to hard clipping. It is used on synths, bass, drums and vocals to add grit, harmonics and aggression. Type chooses the distortion curve, Drive sets how hard the signal is pushed, Bias adds asymmetry for different harmonics, Spread varies the effect between channels, Dynamics preserves more of the input's dynamics, DC Filter removes any DC offset, and Mix blends with the dry signal.
kilohearts|khs distortion.name: kHs Distortion

kilohearts|khs dynamics.about: kHs Dynamics is Kilohearts' combined compressor and expander with separate upper and lower thresholds, so it can compress loud signals and expand or upwardly compress quiet ones. It is used to control dynamic range on drums, bass, vocals and synths, for tightening, squashing or upward compression effects. High Threshold and High Ratio act on signal above the upper threshold, Low Threshold and Low Ratio act on signal below the lower threshold, Attack, Release and Knee set the response, In Gain and Out Gain set levels, and Mix allows parallel processing.
kilohearts|khs dynamics.name: kHs Dynamics

kilohearts|khs ensemble.about: kHs Ensemble is Kilohearts' ensemble effect, which layers several detuned, modulated copies of the signal for a thick, wide unison sound. It is used on pads, synths, strings and guitars. Voices sets the number of copies, Detune sets how far they spread in pitch, Spread sets stereo width, Motion sets how the voices move over time, and Mix blends with the dry signal.
kilohearts|khs ensemble.name: kHs Ensemble

kilohearts|khs filter.about: kHs Filter by Kilohearts is a stereo filter that changes tonal balance by selecting a Type, then using Cutoff, Q, Gain, and Slope to cut or emphasize frequencies. It suits removing rumble or noise, softening harshness, adding resonance, and creating simple frequency contrast in mixes or stems. For common jobs, use Type Low pass with Cutoff around 2-8 kHz to soften highs; use Type High shelf with Cutoff near 2-8 kHz and Gain from -6 to +6 dB to lift or cut highs. Start Q at 0.707 and raise to 2-6 for resonance. Use Slope x1 for gentle roll-off and x4-x6 for steep.
kilohearts|khs filter.name: kHs Filter

kilohearts|khs flanger.about: Kilohearts kHs Flanger is a stereo effect that adds a short modulated delay to create a whooshy, sweeping flanging effect. It is good for adding movement to guitar, keys, pads, and synths, making dull loops feel alive, or creating dramatic sweep accents. Start with Delay 1–3 ms, Depth 1–5 ms, and Rate 0.3–1 Hz for classic whoosh; raise Feedback 40–70% for a deeper dub sound and use Spread 20–40% for stereo width. Set Mix 20–50% to blend subtly, or 100% for a wet effect. Use Offset to phase the L/R modulation and Motion for extra LFO movement.
kilohearts|khs flanger.name: kHs Flanger

kilohearts|khs formant filter.about: kHs Formant Filter is Kilohearts' vowel filter, which imposes vocal formant resonances on any sound to make it talk or sound vowel-like. It is used on synths, bass and drums for vowel sweeps and talking effects, often with X or Y modulated. X and Y move through a two-dimensional vowel space, Q sets how sharp the resonances are, and Lows and Highs set how much of the low and high content outside the formants is kept.
kilohearts|khs formant filter.name: kHs Formant Filter

kilohearts|khs frequency shifter.about: kHs Frequency Shifter is Kilohearts' frequency shifter, which moves every frequency in the signal up or down by the same number of hertz. Unlike pitch shifting this breaks harmonic relationships, so small shifts give phasing or beating movement and large shifts give metallic, inharmonic or dissonant tones. Shift is the only control that matters: small values for subtle motion or stereo detune, larger values for obvious sound-design effects.
kilohearts|khs frequency shifter.name: kHs Frequency Shifter

kilohearts|khs gain.about: kHs Gain is Kilohearts' simple gain utility for raising or lowering the level of a signal without changing its tone. It is used for level matching, gain staging and trimming before or after other effects. Gain sets the amount and mode chooses how it is expressed; Bypass compares with the unprocessed signal.
kilohearts|khs gain.name: kHs Gain

kilohearts|khs gate.about: kHs Gate is a dynamic noise gate that mutes or reduces sound below a Threshold, letting louder parts pass. It is good for removing hum, hiss, and bleed between phrases, tightening drums, and keeping keys or bass clean. For common jobs, set Threshold a few dB above unwanted noise; Range to Inf dB for full muting, lower for soft reduction. Tolerance around +6.00 dB helps the gate open and close smoothly. Use Attack 0.00–5.00 ms for crisp cuts, Hold 25.0–100.0 ms, Release 25.0–100.0 ms, shorter for tight results. Keep Look-ahead On for accurate response on fast transients; leave Flip Off for normal gating and Bypass Off to hear the gate.
kilohearts|khs gate.name: kHs Gate

kilohearts|khs haas.about: kHs Haas is a stereo effect that adds a short, selectable delay to one side of a stereo pair, slightly separating the sides in time to widen and open the image. It is useful for giving width to vocals, synths, drums, loops, or ambience without reverb, and for making a center-heavy track feel less collapsed. Use Bypass Off, Channel to choose Left or Right as the delayed side, and Delay for the amount: start at the default 5 ms, use 1-3 ms for subtle glue, 5-10 ms for a wide but controlled sound, and up to 20-30 ms for a more smeared, spacious result. Always check mono compatibility and keep the delay low enough to avoid comb filtering or timing issues.
kilohearts|khs haas.name: kHs Haas

kilohearts|khs ladder filter.about: kHs Ladder Filter is a stereo analog-style filter that passes lows and mids while cutting highs, adding resonant peaks and warm transistor or diode-like saturation when driven. It is good for sculpting vocals, bass, guitars, synth patches, and mixes, from gentle low-pass coloration to aggressive sweep, growl, and creative effect work. Set Cutoff near 200 Hz to 2 kHz for warm darkening, 500 Hz to 5 kHz for bright sweep, or 8 kHz to 20 kHz for subtle highs. Use Resonance 0 to 40% for peak; 70 to 100% for strong whoosh. Keep Drive at 0 to 6 dB for glue, 10 to 25 dB for grit. Bias toward -50% for softer clipping or +50% for tighter punch. Set Topology to Transistor for smooth color or Diode for sharper edge; turn Saturate On only for extra saturation. Use Bypass Off.
kilohearts|khs ladder filter.name: kHs Ladder Filter

kilohearts|khs limiter.about:
kHs Limiter is Kilohearts' brickwall limiter that stops peaks from crossing its threshold and uses input/output gain to balance the limited signal.
It is good for masters, drums, vocals, and mixing when you need to control peaks, add gentle loudness, or prevent digital clipping.
Start with Input gain at 0 dB, pull it down 3–6 dB before limiting, set Threshold near your peaks (about −1 to 0 dB for masters), then restore level with Output gain, usually +2 to +8 dB.
Use Release around 10–20 ms for natural material, 5–10 ms for punchy drums, and 30–100 ms for smoother masters; check Bypass to confirm the effect.
kilohearts|khs limiter.name: kHs Limiter

kilohearts|khs nonlinear filter.about: kHs Nonlinear Filter is Kilohearts' resonant multimode filter with built-in drive, so pushing it adds saturation inside the filter. It is used for warm or aggressive filtering of synths, bass and drums and for filter sweeps that grow gritty with resonance. Filter Type chooses the response (low-pass, high-pass, band-pass, notch and others), Cutoff and Q set frequency and resonance, Drive sets how hard the filter is pushed, and Mode chooses the saturation behavior.
kilohearts|khs nonlinear filter.name: kHs Nonlinear Filter

kilohearts|khs phase distortion.about: kHs Phase Distortion is Kilohearts' phase-distortion effect, which modulates the phase of the signal using the signal itself (or a sidechain input), creating harmonics and distortion that sound different from ordinary clipping. It is used for adding edge, buzz and movement to synths, bass and drums. Drive sets the amount of phase modulation, Tone filters the modulating signal, Bias offsets the effect for asymmetric harmonics, Spread varies it between channels, Normalize compensates level, and Mix blends with the dry signal.
kilohearts|khs phase distortion.name: kHs Phase Distortion

kilohearts|khs phaser.about: kHs Phaser is a stereo modulation effect from Kilohearts that sweeps a set of all-pass filters to create a smooth, watery phasing movement in the sound. It is good for adding movement to guitars, synths, pads, and drums, widening stereo images, and making rhythmic or ambient textures.
