Use Makeup Gain to restore level; turn Sidechain on only when another signal should trigger the compression.
torqwave|compressor.name: Compressor

torqwave|convolution reverb.about: Torqwave Convolution Reverb is a built-in stereo reverb effect that convolves the audio with an impulse response and blends the resulting reflected tail with the original sound. It is good for adding a sense of room, hall, or space to vocals, drums, guitars, or loops, making dry recordings sound more natural, widening tight mixes, and creating short ambience or longer atmospheric tails. The main parameter is Mix, ranging from 0% to 100%, with 0% fully dry and 100% fully wet; the 30% default is a useful starting point for natural blends, 15–35% for subtle space, 40–70% for a more obvious reverb presence, and 80–100% when the reverb should dominate.
torqwave|convolution reverb.name: Convolution Reverb

torqwave|de-esser.about: Torqwave's built-in De-esser is a Dynamics effect that lowers sibilant peaks in a selected high-frequency band, leaving the rest of the sound mostly untouched. It is good for taming harsh “s” and “sh” sounds on vocals, narration, or dialogue so consonants do not spike the mix. For common jobs, set Frequency near 6000 Hz, dropping it if the sibilance is dark or raising it if it is very bright. Set Threshold around -30 dB and raise it until only obvious sibilants are controlled. Use Reduction from 6 to 12 dB for subtle clean-up, or up to 18 dB for very harsh voices. Keep Turn Down on The high band for natural results; use The whole sound only if the full voice still feels harsh. Leave Linear Phase Off and use Listen to audition the affected band.
torqwave|de-esser.name: De-esser

torqwave|dynamic eq.about: Dynamic EQ is Torqwave's built-in stereo effect that applies EQ whose gain changes with signal level, taming or boosting chosen frequency ranges only as they get loud or quiet. It is good for cleaning resonant mids, controlling bass rumble, softening harsh peaks, and adding presence without constant tonal coloring. For common jobs, use Band 1 On, Band 3 On, and Band 5 On; set each band's Shape, Frequency, Q, Gain, Mode, Threshold, Ratio, Attack, and Release. For reducing loud trouble spots, use Mode Over, Threshold -30 dB, Ratio 4:1, Attack 10 ms, Release 150 ms. Try Band 1 Low Shelf 100 Hz for sub control, Band 3 Bell 1000 Hz Q 2 Gain -6 dB for boxy mids, Band 5 High Shelf 8000 Hz for air. Use Output for make-up level.
torqwave|dynamic eq.name: Dynamic EQ

torqwave|exciter.about: Exciter is a built-in stereo saturation effect that adds harmonics to low, mid, and high bands, thickening the sound and adding warmth, punch, or edge depending on drive. It is good for warming bass, drums, vocals, and guitars, making quiet material louder and more present, or gluing a mix with subtle distortion. Set Low Crossover near 200 Hz and High Crossover near 3000 Hz to separate bands. Start with Low Drive at 2-6 dB for bass warmth, Mid Drive at 3-8 dB for body, and High Drive at 2-6 dB for sparkle. Choose Low Curve, Mid Curve, and High Curve as Tape for smoothness, Tube for balanced character, or Transistor for aggression. Keep Low Mix, Mid Mix, and High Mix near 100% for full saturation or 40-80% to blend. Trim Output around -3 to 0 dB, and try Linear Phase On for tighter phase.
torqwave|exciter.name: Exciter

torqwave|flanger.about: Torqwave Flanger is a built-in stereo modulation effect that sweeps a very short modulated delay through the signal, creating a comb-filtered, watery whoosh. It is good for vocals, guitars, synths, drum loops, and sweep or riser moments. Rate controls sweep speed, about 0.05-0.25 Hz for subtle movement and 1-5 Hz for dramatic flanging. Delay sets the base delay, usually 1-8 ms, while Depth sets the modulation amount, usually 2-10 ms for clean flanging and higher values for smear. Feedback around 0.40-0.70 adds resonance; near 0.95 can self-oscillate. Mix 20-50% is subtle, 60-100% is strong. Stereo Spread 60-120 degrees widens the effect.
torqwave|flanger.name: Flanger

torqwave|graphic eq (10 bands).about:
Graphic EQ (10 Bands) is Torqwave's built-in stereo 10-band graphic equalizer that raises or lowers ten fixed frequency bands by up to ±12 dB.
It is good for broad tonal shaping, cleaning muddy or boomy material, adding warmth or brightness, and taming harsh highs or room rumble.
Most common jobs: 31.5 Hz and 63 Hz for sub-bass control, usually -6 to +3 dB; 125 Hz and 250 Hz for body and mud, -6 to +2 dB; 500 Hz and 1000 Hz for warmth, -4 to +3 dB; 2000 Hz and 4000 Hz for presence and clarity, -3 to +6 dB; 8000 Hz and 16000 Hz for air, -6 to +6 dB.
torqwave|graphic eq (10 bands).name: Graphic EQ (10 Bands)

torqwave|graphic eq (31 bands).about: Torqwave's built-in 31-band graphic equalizer shapes tone by boosting or cutting fixed frequency bands from 20 Hz to 20 kHz. It is good for overall balance, correcting muddy low mids, taming rumbles, adding presence, or matching a track. Use 20 Hz, 25 Hz, 31.5 Hz, 40 Hz, 50 Hz, and 63 Hz at -2 to +2 dB for sub and kick low end; 100 Hz, 125 Hz, and 160 Hz at -2 to +1 dB for warmth; 500 Hz, 630 Hz, and 800 Hz at 0 to -3 dB to reduce mud; 2000 Hz and 4000 Hz at +1 to +3 dB for presence; 10000 Hz, 12500 Hz, 16000 Hz, and 20000 Hz at +1 to +4 dB for air; leave other bands at 0 dB.
torqwave|graphic eq (31 bands).name: Graphic EQ (31 Bands)

torqwave|limiter.about: Torqwave's built-in Limiter is a stereo dynamics effect that pulls down any signal that rises above its Ceiling and lets you set Gain and how fast it recovers with Release. Use it to protect against clipping, keep transients in check, or raise overall loudness while preserving peaks, especially for final masters, podcast narration, or dialogue. Ceiling is the maximum output level, usually -1 dBFS for digital safety or 0 dBFS for a hotter final signal. Gain sets level, typically 0 dB first, then +2 to +6 dB if the result sounds quiet after limiting. Release is recovery time, around 20-100 ms for speech, 50-200 ms for music, and 1-10 ms only for very short spikes.
torqwave|limiter.name: Limiter

torqwave|maximizer.about: Torqwave Maximizer is a built-in dynamics maximizer that raises overall loudness by limiting peaks to a ceiling, with optional gain and transient shaping. It is good for masters, podcasts, mixes, or any stem needing a louder, fuller result without exceeding a target level. For common jobs, set Ceiling near -1.00 dBTP for digital masters, or -2.00 to -3.00 dBTP for extra headroom. Use Gain for the amount of boost: 0.00 for safety, 3.00–6.00 dB for typical mastering, 10.00–15.00 dB only when the source has headroom. Choose Character Balanced by default, Transparent for gentle limiting, or Loud for aggressive compression. Increase Transient Emphasis from 0.00% when drums or speech sound dull, often 20.00–50.00%.
torqwave|maximizer.name: Maximizer

torqwave|multiband compressor.about: Torqwave's Multiband Compressor is a built-in Dynamics effect that splits the stereo signal into low, mid, and high bands and reduces peaks in each band. It suits bass control, smoothing mids, taming harsh highs, and raising loudness. Set Low Crossover near 200 Hz and High Crossover near 2000 Hz, or match the material. For bass, Low Threshold -20 dB, Low Ratio 4:1, Low Attack 10 ms, Low Release 100 ms, Low Makeup 0 to 3 dB. For mids, Mid Threshold -20 dB, Mid Ratio 2 to 4:1, Mid Attack 10 ms, Mid Release 100 ms. For highs, High Threshold -20 dB, High Ratio 2 to 4:1, High Attack 10 ms, High Release 100 ms. Raise Output for level; leave Linear Phase Off unless needed.
torqwave|multiband compressor.name: Multiband Compressor

torqwave|multiband stereo width.about: Multiband Stereo Width is Torqwave's built-in stereo effect that widens or narrows separate low, mid, and high frequency bands, making a sound broader, tighter, or mono. It is good for widening guitars, synths, pads, ambience, and vocals, or keeping bass and lead vocals narrow for playback compatibility. Start with Low Crossover around 120-250 Hz and High Crossover around 2-5 kHz, set Low Width to 0-70% to protect the low end, Mid Width to 100-140% for a natural spread, and High Width to 100-160% for air; use Linear Phase On only if you notice smearing.
torqwave|multiband stereo width.name: Multiband Stereo Width

torqwave|parametric eq.about: Parametric EQ is Torqwave's built-in five-band equalizer that boosts or cuts chosen frequency bands, filters low or high content, and can process Stereo, Mid, Side, Left, or Right channels, with a Linear Phase option. It is good for removing rumble, cutting mud, controlling resonances, and brightening recordings. For common jobs, set Band 1 Type to Low Shelf or High-Pass around 30 to 80 Hz for bass control. Use Band 2 Type as Bell near 200 to 400 Hz with negative Gain to reduce muddiness; set Channel to Mid if only center mud. Use Band 3 Type as Bell near 1000 Hz, Band 4 Type as Bell near 3000 Hz for clarity, and Band 5 Type as High Shelf around 8 kHz for air. Use low Q for broad changes and high Q for narrow fixes; turn unused bands Off.
torqwave|parametric eq.name: Parametric EQ

torqwave|phaser.about: Torqwave's built-in Phaser is a stereo modulation effect that sweeps multiple all-pass filter stages through the band between Low Frequency and High Frequency, creating moving notches and a watery phase shift in the sound. It is good for making electric guitars, basses, synths, vocals, and drum loops sound swirling, spacious, or slightly unstable. For typical jobs set Rate near 0.25–0.75 Hz for slow movement or up to 2–3 Hz for faster swirl; keep Low Frequency around 200–600 Hz and High Frequency around 1000–5000 Hz for musical phasing. Use Stages 4–6 for clarity, 8–12 for thicker phase; Feedback 0.20–0.45 for resonance, higher for stronger resonance. Mix 30–60% blends effect with dry; Stereo Spread 60–120 deg gives wide movement.
torqwave|phaser.name: Phaser

torqwave|reverb.about: Torqwave Reverb is Torqwave's built-in stereo reverb that adds a reflected tail and ambience to a dry sound. It is good for making dry voices, drums, guitars, or stems sound less dead, placing them in a room, hall, or larger space, and creating consistent spaces in mixes. Key parameters: Pre-Delay 5-25 ms for natural lead separation, 20 ms default works well; Decay 0.5-2 s for tight rooms or drums, 2-5 s for vocals, 5-10 s for larger washes; Size 100% for balanced space, lower for small rooms, higher for larger halls; Damping 20-50% to tame high-frequency harshness, higher for darker plate-like tails; Width 100% for full stereo, lower for mono-safe or more focused; Mix 15-35% for subtle support, 40-70% for larger effect, 100% for insert-only or sends if preferred.
torqwave|reverb.name: Reverb

torqwave|transient shaper.about: Torqwave's Transient Shaper is a built-in stereo Dynamics effect that increases or reduces the attack and sustain sections of a sound in separate low, mid, and high bands. It is useful for tightening drums, adding punch to bass or vocals, softening harsh transients, and controlling sustain in guitar or synth material. Low Crossover and High Crossover set the band edges; start at 200 Hz and 3000 Hz, or move High Crossover to 5000 to 8000 Hz for cymbal work. Low Attack, Low Sustain, Mid Attack, Mid Sustain, High Attack, and High Sustain are set in dB, typically -6 to +6 dB; try +2 to +4 dB attack with -1 to -2 dB sustain for punch, or -1 to -3 dB high attack for taming. Output trims level, usually 0 to +3 dB. Linear Phase is best left Off unless timing issues appear.
torqwave|transient shaper.name: Transient Shaper

zynaptiq|intensity.about: Zynaptiq INTENSITY is a detail and clarity enhancer that brings out hidden detail, texture and density in audio using perceptual processing rather than ordinary EQ or compression. It is good for making mixes, masters, vocals, drums and dull recordings sound clearer, denser and more present. INTENSITY sets the amount of processing and MIX blends it with the dry signal, BIAS and BIAS CURVE PRESET tilt the effect toward certain frequency ranges (BAND 0 to BAND 8 hold the curve), and LEVEL COMPENSATION keeps the loudness comparable for fair A/B checks. Small amounts are often enough; high settings can sound harsh.
zynaptiq|intensity.name: INTENSITY

zynaptiq|morph.about: Zynaptiq MORPH is a stereo effect that morphs and crossfades between two inputs, shifting timbre and texture as it moves from one source to the other. It is good for sound design, blending takes or synths, building evolving textures, stereo transitions, and hybrid timbres with integrated reverb. Start MIX IN A and MIX IN B at 0 dB, balance them, and set MIX AxB near 0 dB. Move MORPH INDEX from 0.00 toward 1.00 to shift from A to B; use X-FADE for a plain crossfade feel. Choose ALGORITHM SELECT as CLASSIC for smooth morphs or INTERWEAVE (LL) for denser detail. Keep COMPLEXITY near 1.00 for full texture, set FORMANTS around 0.50 for a neutral tone, and leave AMP SENSE near 1.00. Add a small REVERB MIX with mid REVERB SIZE and DAMPING for glue.
zynaptiq|morph.name: MORPH

zynaptiq|morph sc.about: Zynaptiq MORPH SC is the sidechain version of MORPH, which morphs in real time between two audio sources, the main input (A) and a sidechain input (B), creating hybrid sounds rather than a simple crossfade. It is good for sound design, blending two instruments or a voice and an instrument into one hybrid, and morphing transitions. MORPH INDEX moves the result from A to B, ALGORITHM SELECT chooses the morphing method, and FORMANTS, AMP SENSE and COMPLEXITY shape how the sources combine. MIX IN A, MIX IN B, SOLO A and SOLO B balance and check the sources, ALIGN helps when the two are not time-aligned, and REVERB MIX adds space.
zynaptiq|morph sc.name: MORPH SC

zynaptiq|orange vocoder.about: Zynaptiq ORANGE VOCODER is a vocoder with a built-in polyphonic synth carrier, its own effects and pitch quantization, used to make a voice or other modulator sound like a synth or robot. It is good for classic and modern vocoder vocals, talking synths, choir-like pads and pitched robotic speech. SYNTH ON and VOCODER ON enable the carrier synth and vocoder, VOCODER ALGORITHM chooses the vocoder type, and FORMANT SHIFT and UNVOICED LEVEL control character and the clarity of consonants. MIX VOICE LEVEL, MIX VOCODER LEVEL and MIX CARRIER LEVEL balance the dry voice, vocoder and carrier, PITCH-Q ON quantizes pitch without MIDI, and REVERB ON and CHORUS ON add space and width.
zynaptiq|orange vocoder.name: ORANGE VOCODER

zynaptiq|orange vocoder sc.about: Zynaptiq ORANGE VOCODER SC is the sidechain version of ORANGE VOCODER, so an external signal can be used as the carrier or modulator instead of only the built-in synth. It is good for vocoding a voice with an existing synth or instrument track, talking instruments and robotic vocals. FLIP INPUTS swaps which input is carrier and which is modulator, VOCODER ALGORITHM chooses the vocoder type, and FORMANT SHIFT and UNVOICED LEVEL control character and consonant clarity. MIX VOICE LEVEL, MIX VOCODER LEVEL and MIX CARRIER LEVEL set the balance, and REVERB ON and CHORUS ON add space and width.
zynaptiq|orange vocoder sc.name: ORANGE VOCODER SC
